issue_context.title: Callback plugins will crash if a module returns exception=None
issue_context.body:
### Summary

If a module calls `fail_json()` and provides `exception=None`, this will crash every callback that uses `_handle_exception` from `CallbackBase`: if verbosity is < 3, it will try to call `split` on `None`, and otherwise it will try to concatenate a string with `None` (which results in `TypeError`).

review_comments: this conversion should not be done here, but when the result is first processed ... also I would consider it a bug of the module emitting such a result

Since this is a function that's directly called by other callback plugins, I don't see how this can be achieved except by convention. And preventing crashes by hoping that all parts (including a lot of code not part of this repository) sticks to convention is a bit extreme IMO.

Not what i meant, to clarify, this should issue an error in 'result processing' in  executor/ and not at the callback. It will not depend on the external code, but it will point out that it has a bug that should be reported and fixed
